title: Blockscout — one explorer token-information installation

task.name: Buy and recover useful token information from the selected explorer
task.purpose: Let an independent customer application retrieve the selected explorer's token information under an agreed per-request price, then use and recover the exact response with its original payment and usage history.
task.request: One selected explorer origin, EVM chain and token-information endpoint family. Use the original /{chain_id}/api/v2/tokens/{address_hash} contract where it matches the selected source, with the actual configured PRO or operator-instance authentication and quota/error behavior. Review the actual Stellar payment network, asset, recipient, atomic price and permitted task budget before the original purchase.
task.completeOutput: The original provider JSON is downloaded by the customer with its complete selected request, payment/recovery identity and usage record. The private operator sees the same response, limits and attempt history. Deliver the installed merchant, private desk, complete reviewed connection/deployment package, Node and Python consumers, source, retained state and a reopened receiving installation.
task.repeatTrigger: The participating customer's actual monitoring, application or analysis needs another token-information result. Retain each useful later purchase and its customer operation; a retry/recovery reuses its original purchase.
task.pricedUnit: One agreed token-information response for the selected chain/address route. Preserve the merchant's integer atomic price and original provider credit/quota contract; retain the EVM data chain separately from the Stellar payment network.

source.reference: Selected original explorer connection and complete installed source: stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/blockscout-stellar-pro-api/. Select the actual PRO or approved operator-instance connection through the maintained connection review.
source.population: The selected explorer's token-information endpoint family and authorized chain, with the exact original provider JSON, request, original account usage, paid delivery and customer recovery history.
source.meaning: Preserve provider numeric strings and null values, chain/address identity and bridge-origin data. Validate the selected route before payment. Keep explorer chain ID distinct from stellar:testnet or stellar:pubnet and local merchant limits distinct from the upstream provider's actual quota.
source.changePolicy: The selected operator approves source origin, API authentication reference, account, indexed chain, price and limits in the original connection review. Credential rotation retains original account history; a different provider account uses its actual separate state. Retain prior source/response and deployment history.

receiving.application: Original Blockscout connection setup and Blockscout token merchant Applications entries, private operator/usage desk, original Node/Python customers and complete source. Linux with Node 24+, Python 3.11+ and flock.
receiving.acceptanceRule: The selected actual API request/authentication returns its exact original JSON; the agreed testnet purchase recovers that response; both Node/Python consumers address the same installation; the operator explains actual usage/limit behavior; saved-state stop/reopen preserves delivery/history; the receiving engineer uses the complete source/configuration package and completes the agreed correction.
receiving.changeAndWithdraw: The customer/prime controls production rollout and resale terms. The original operator reviews changes and challenge-only/paid activation in the same saved application, keeps private desk access separate from the seller listener, and can pause the retained merchant.
receiving.recovery: Recover the original customer intent and native attempt after interruption. Reopen the same reviewed deployment/state; retain original response and accounting history. Receive/export the complete connection package and restore the actual provider database through its original backup operation.
receiving.maintenance: Name the provider-account owner, deployment/credential operator, payment authority, integration engineer, customer acceptance owner and receiving engineer. Retain source/dependency versions, usage/cost ownership, the agreed correction allowance and rollback/incident route.

steps.title: Bind the selected explorer and customer task
steps.result: Retain the original relationship/workshare. Select actual origin, chain, token route, authentication, response/quota contract, data rights, customer use and private receiving host.

steps.title: Prepare and receive the complete provider connection
steps.result: Open the original Blockscout connection setup, review the source/target/account/payment selections and prepare its whole deployment. Start with the existing challenge-only lifecycle; select paid activation under the actual merchant authority.

steps.title: Install operator and language consumers
steps.result: Use the original merchant state, private usage/response desk and Node/Python customers. Bind the complete request and response download to their original customer intent and payment.

steps.title: Operate purchase, limits and recovery
steps.result: Run the selected actual testnet journey and agreed upstream limit behavior, recover the original response after interruption and stop/reopen the same state. Keep actual provider response and quota findings with the installation.

steps.title: Complete receiving and useful repeated use
steps.result: Receive source/dependencies, reviewed connection/deployment package, both consumers, complete saved state and runbook. Complete the original review round and let the selected independent operator run later useful tasks.

inputs: Original customer/prime case, selected explorer customer and accountable integration/acceptance owner
Current original Workshare edition, complete commissioning inputs and receiving packet
Actual authorized explorer origin, chain, route, authentication method and credential reference
Original permitted response examples, numeric/null semantics, account quota/errors and data-use rights
Merchant and independent buyer deployment IDs from the original SF47 case
Actual Stellar network/asset/recipient, atomic price, budget, spending authority and facilitator selections
Linux receiving host, private state/application paths, Node/Python dependencies and engineer
Provider/hosting/usage cost owner, actual activation/release decision and maintenance/rollback responsibility
